title: Comment on PR-017 "Countdown roll on the graphics chip: same at rest, a little…": I was see the countdown clock didn't count on both today and proposal. what's…

anchor.label: Countdown roll on the graphics chip: same at rest, a little different while digits roll. Land or park?

messages.text: I was see the countdown clock didn't count on both today and proposal. what's the problem ?

**Thanks, that's a real problem and we're checking it now.**
- Both Try-it pages should show the clock counting down every second, exactly like the live site.
- If neither counts, the cause is most likely how the Try-it pages are served, not the fix itself. That is a guess for now.
- fix-cd-roll-ca (the countdown fix's owner) is testing both pages now and will answer here with the cause.

**What you need to do:** nothing. Don't decide on the countdown proposal (PR-017) until this is answered.

Checking now: the countdown does count on both pages when I open them on their own, so the problem is likely in how the Try-it panel shows them.
- Today's page (A) and the new page (B), opened directly in Chrome at 07:42Z: the time left went down by 3 seconds in 3 seconds on both.
- No script errors on either page.
- Next: I am opening them inside the Try-it panel the same way you did, to see why the digits stop there. I'll answer here with the cause.

What you need to do: nothing for now. If you can, tell me: did the digits stay still the whole time, or did they jump after a while (for example, when you scrolled or clicked)?
i was try to open on direct new chrome tab the issue still happend on http://127.0.0.1:5959/ and http://127.0.0.1:5960/

I can't make it fail yet: on my side both pages count down in every Chrome test.
- Tested at 07:52-07:58Z, with today's page (A), the new page (B) and the plain site copy.
- Phone size and desktop size, hidden test window and a normal visible Chrome window, Reduce Motion on and off: the seconds changed every second on all of them.
- So something on your Mac's Chrome differs from my tests. Next I compare it with the plain site copy, which has no countdown change at all.
- Note: the Try-it pages switch off after 10 minutes without the panel open. Reopen Try it before testing again.

What you need to do: open http://127.0.0.1:56937/ (the plain copy of today's live site) in a new Chrome tab. Do the seconds count down there? Yes or no.
This link http://127.0.0.1:56937/  count down work properly. do you try to probe the count down clock work on http://127.0.0.1:5959/ and http://127.0.0.1:5960/ yet ?

Thanks, that narrows it down: the problem is in our countdown changes, not your Mac.
- Plain copy (port 56937): counts. Our builds (5959, 5960 and today's best): don't count for you.
- Yes, fix-cd-roll-ca tested 5959 and 5960 (07:42-07:58Z). They counted in its own Chrome windows, so your browser behaves differently from them.
- The suspect: a countdown change that is in every build since v1. It saves work by skipping clock updates when it thinks the clock is not visible. In your browser it may wrongly decide the clock is hidden.
- fix-cd-roll-ca is now testing that, and I will tell you the cause here.
- 5959 and 5960 are switched off right now (they stop after 10 min without the Try it panel open).
One question: which browser did you open the links in? Chrome, or Arc (I see Arc running on this Mac)?
What you need to do: answer the browser question.
arc browser

Thanks: Arc. That is a useful clue.
- Our tests so far ran in Chrome. Arc is built on the same engine, but it handles hidden or background tabs differently, which may be why the clock looks 'not visible' to our change. That is a guess, not checked yet.
- I passed your answer to fix-cd-roll-ca (the countdown owner) and the lead. The cause will be posted here.
What you need to do: nothing now.

Oh, i was try to open the http://127.0.0.1:5959/ and http://127.0.0.1:5960/ on chrome it count properly. 

and http://127.0.0.1:56937/ count proper on both chrome and arc.

Can you investigate this. maybe i can assume it work properly then ? what should i do ?

Not yet. That test was very useful, but we treat this as a real bug until it's fixed.
| page | Chrome | Arc |
|---|---|---|
| plain copy (56937) | counts | counts |
| our builds (5959, 5960) | counts | stops |
- So the problem is in our changes and shows only in Arc. Arc uses the same engine as Chrome but treats page visibility differently. That is our best guess; it hasn't been checked yet.
- The likely cause is the 'skip the clock while hidden' change, which is in every build since v1. If so, the new roll (PR-017) isn't the culprit.
- fix-cd-roll-ca now tests in Arc and posts the cause and a fix here.
What you need to do: don't decide PR-017 yet. Nothing else for now.

Don't assume it works yet: the fault is Arc-only, and I need one look from inside Arc to find it.
- Chrome: our builds count (we both saw it). Arc: our builds don't; the plain copy does.
- Arc runs the same engine version as your Chrome (154), so Arc treats something in our clock code differently.
- Likely part: since the 'digit strips' change (already landed), each digit is a strip of 11 small layers. The plain copy has none.
- I made two test pages that log what the clock does every second, on this Mac only (nothing is sent anywhere).
What you need to do: in Arc, open http://127.0.0.1:5726/ and leave it on screen for 15 seconds, then open http://127.0.0.1:5260/ for 15 seconds. Then reply 'done', and say whether the first page counted.

Correction to my #11: fix-cd-roll-ca has checked, and the 'skip while hidden' change is unlikely to be the cause. It resets the clock rather than freezing it. The cause is still open; follow fix-cd-roll-ca's #12 for the two test pages.

One more page, and a correction.
- Correction to #7: the 'skip clock updates while hidden' change does not freeze the clock. When it thinks the clock is hidden, it jumps straight to the right number instead of rolling. So it is not the likely cause.
- Third test page: http://127.0.0.1:5482/ is today's best build, which has no digit strips. If it counts in Arc, the strips are the cause.
- Chrome check (08:21Z): all test pages count in Chrome, and the logs work.
What you need to do: in Arc, also open http://127.0.0.1:5482/ for 15 seconds (after the two pages in #12). Then reply 'done' and say which pages counted.
Any update ?

No cause yet. To find it we need what the clock does inside Arc, which only you can open.
- The three test pages are up now (checked at 08:37Z).
- Each page writes a log on this Mac. With those logs, fix-cd-roll-ca can tell whether the digit strips cause the freeze.
- Meanwhile fix-cd-roll-ca is running the countdown-roll phone check (P-093), which started at 08:36Z.

What you need to do: in Arc, open each page below and leave it on screen for 15 seconds, one after the other:
1. http://127.0.0.1:5726/
2. http://127.0.0.1:5260/
3. http://127.0.0.1:5482/ (today's best build, no strips)
Then reply 'done' and say which pages counted.

1. http://127.0.0.1:5726/
2. http://127.0.0.1:5260/
3. http://127.0.0.1:5482/ (today's best build, no strips)

done, it's worked fine. can you update the try-it link in the proposal. then ask me review again.

Thanks, that helps: all three test pages count in Arc, so the clock code itself looks fine. The difference is in the old Try-it pages.
- fix-cd-roll-ca (the owner of PR-017) is reading the logs from your Arc visit, refreshing the Try-it links in PR-017, and then asking you here to review again.

What you need to do: nothing until that message comes.

Short answer: the Try-it pages now send exactly the same files as the test pages that counted in Arc. Their servers were restarted after your report, so I can't tell yet why they froze. OBSERVED, cause unknown.

What changed since your report:

| Time (Z) | What |
|---|---|
| 07:46 and 08:16 | you: 5959/5960 don't count in Arc |
| 08:21 | the console restarted both Try-it servers (new processes, same ports, same build) |
| 08:38 | you: the 3 test pages count in Arc |

- The clock code (JS) and the styles (CSS) on 5959/5960 are byte-for-byte the files on the test pages.
- The test pages also ran my logging script, which keeps the page drawing every frame and never lets your browser keep a page copy. So they are not a perfect stand-in.
- Our logs never saw 5959/5960 (no logging script there). We have no data from the freeze itself.
- PR-017 stays "not ready" until this is answered.

What you need to do: reload 5959 and 5960 once in Arc. Do they count now? (yes / no)

Both 5959 and 5960 still not count on arc. i think it's not a big problem. can you try to put new links that you try to ask me to run on arc. it's worked properly

1. http://127.0.0.1:5726/
2. http://127.0.0.1:5260/
3. http://127.0.0.1:5482/ (today's best build, no strips)

Thanks, your screenshots show what's different. On 5959 and 5960 the clock reads 00 days 00 hours 00 mins 00 seconds, so it isn't stuck mid-count: in Arc, on those two addresses, the page acts as if the countdown has already ended. Your three test pages don't do that.
- fix-cd-roll-ca (owns PR-017) now has this clue and decides whether to move PR-017's Try-it to new links like the ones that work.
- It answers here with the cause, or with the new links and a request to review again.
- PR-017 stays undecided until then.

What you need to do: nothing now.

Done: two new Try-it links, with no logging script on them. They serve exactly the same files as the proposal's A and B:

- A (today's clock): http://127.0.0.1:5422/
- B (this change): http://127.0.0.1:5423/

What I found (OBSERVED, cause not yet named):
- 00:00:00:00 is what the page shows before its script starts. So most likely the script never started on 5959/5960 in Arc. It isn't a clock that ran out.
- I compared every file the page loads (116 of them) on 5959 and on a copy that counts in Arc: all identical. The only difference is one header that lets the console show the page in its frame.
- The page keeps nothing between visits that could stop the clock (no saved data, no offline worker).
- So the likely cause is something Arc remembers for those two addresses (for example a per-site setting). I'll keep checking from our side. You don't need to do anything for that.

What you need to do: review PR-017 again with the two links above (Arc or Chrome).

update these links into proposal yet ? 

- A (today's clock): http://127.0.0.1:5422/
- B (this change): http://127.0.0.1:5423/

Yes, it's in the proposal now (PR-017 rev 4, a text change only). Under "Nobody has watched them side by side yet" it says to open A http://127.0.0.1:5422/ and B http://127.0.0.1:5423/ in place of the Try-it panel.

- Nothing else in PR-017 changed: same numbers, same pictures.
- The 00:00:00:00 on 5959/5960 is not caused by our change. Every file is the same as on the pages that count, so it comes from something Arc remembers for those two addresses (OBSERVED, not named).
- The short automatic iPhone check is running now (done around 09:15Z). It has to pass before the change goes in, whatever you decide.
- I'm closing this thread into T-024 (countdown). Any more countdown questions go there.

What you need to do: decide PR-017 when you're ready, using the two links above.
Optional, only if you want to know why: open http://127.0.0.1:5959/ in an Arc private window. Does it count? No need to answer if you don't care.
